text: Taeo woke to an empty spot beside his bed. Nib was gone. His blanket had been folded into a neat square, and his mug was washed.
Nib had gone straight to Ryu Survey. He showed Minho's mother, Seonhee, his new identification card. He was a person on paper now, and he wanted work inside a gate.
Seonhee gave him tea while Minho slept on the office bench. She warned that he was going blue. Nib corrected her: 'I'm green.'
Taeo burst through the door with one sleeve on and toothpaste on his face. He demanded a note. Nib said he had folded the blanket.
The shouting woke Minho. When he asked who was responsible, Nib immediately pointed at Taeo. There was no hesitation about that report.
Nib wanted the gate with white stone in Chae's photograph. Ryu Survey had won its survey contract: an E-grade gate in the Line 6 tunnel. They entered at ten.
Seonhee pointed out that Minho had bid low. He said they always did. Behind her, Bluebird's notices covered the board, including a final notice.
Minho offered Nib sixty thousand won for the day as a spotter. He would walk ahead, watch for danger, and tell the others what he found.
The subway company hired a clear team, which hired Ryu Survey, which paid Nib. Nib asked who he paid. Nobody, Minho admitted. Nib went first.
Taeo protested the rate, but Nib stopped him. He could count for himself. Sixty thousand won meant three of the yard jobs he already knew.
Seonhee explained that Nib's contract included insurance. Dokgo's porters earned ninety thousand without it. If they broke a leg, treatment came out of their own pockets.
Nib signed his own contract. Two weeks with Eunchae's flashcards had brought him far enough to write his name himself.
Taeo's role was unpaid training beside Haein at the radio table outside. Nib objected that work deserved pay. Minho promised wages when Taeo could do the job.
Minho's father, Dongsik, told Taeo that waiting was the job, and nobody paid for it. A medic arrived with her coffee and disagreed: 'They pay me.'
Im Sejin charged three hundred thousand won to wait at the entrance, or six hundred thousand if she entered. Either way, she was home by six.
The insurer required medical examinations. Asked whether Nib needed one despite being summoned, Sejin answered simply: 'Summoned is not a diagnosis.'
She asked Nib to open his mouth. He said, 'You first.' Sejin obliged, and the examination proceeded with both of them saying ah.
Sejin found scars Nib had stitched himself, badly, because nobody else had been there. Next time, she told him, there would be her. Three hundred thousand a day.
At eight ten, Minho started the compulsory safety film. Haein and the crew had seen it before. For Taeo and Nib, every rule was new.
Crossing into a gate gave each person a return mark. It worked once, and only for the journey back out.
When the boss died, the gate's rim flashed and entry closed. A conscious entrant could then press the mark to return immediately.
Thirty seconds after the boss died, the mark automatically returned its bearer, even unconscious. Anything worn or carried came along too.
The veterans recited the luggage rule from memory. Then came the limits: marks neither healed nor revived. Natives who had never crossed had no mark. Dongsik's hands rested on his wheelchair rims.
Nib would receive a mark because he was entering from Seoul. That meant it would bring him back to Seoul, not to the post he wanted to find.
Until the boss died, entrants had to walk out themselves. Anyone unable to walk waited for a clear team. Dongsik quietly said he had waited nine hours.
In the van, Taeo asked whether matching white stone would help Nib find his post. Nib said it would tell him where to look.
They reached the subway maintenance tunnel. Haein set up the radio table near the violet gate, and Sejin took her place a few metres behind.
The site warden initially counted Nib as a construct. His registration corrected her: three people and one construct. This time, the paperwork counted him properly.
The wooden hauling mule followed the spotter. Its lease cost thirty thousand won monthly. Nib calculated that his day rate was two months of mule. Taeo wished he hadn't.
Nib refused the offered boots.
Sejin backed his bare feet. Taeo took his unpaid clipboard and counted the difference between scouting, medical standby, and his own role.
A radio test dissolved into static across the threshold. The crew planned to return after forty minutes. Nib pointed out that he had no watch.
Taeo approached the frame despite his fear and knocked twice. Nib would be ahead of everyone. Taeo wanted something to come back, even a sound.
Sejin said sound could pass through at close range. Taeo made a code: two knocks from outside meant come back; three from inside meant coming.
Nib compared it to Taeo's talking app. Minho approved the plan. If the team had not returned after forty minutes, Taeo would knock.
Taeo immediately added more warnings. Nib interrupted with the code, repeated correctly. Taeo stopped and apologised. Nib had understood him the first time.
The spotter went first. Taeo realised he was blocking the entrance and stepped aside. Haein would start the clock when Nib crossed.
Before leaving, Nib deliberately pressed his palm to the steel frame. Taeo felt the answering amber pulse in his own hand.
Nib stepped through, a white return mark closing around his wrist. Grandpa had warned Taeo never to enter. He hadn't explained what to do when someone else did.
The mule followed Nib through, and Minho stepped up behind it. Taeo held out his trembling hand. The amber pulse went dark.
